title: Built with AI
text: Most of what you see and hear here was built with AI: the pictures, the music and much of the code.
source: PAGOURO_PLAY/README.md (pictures by Pagouro BE, music by Pagouro Salon); PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/facts.json (made_by: Eric Wade, with Claude)

title: Painted From the Public Domain
text: Every picture in this puzzle was drawn by Pagouro BE, a small model that learned its style from about 3,000 public-domain posters and prints.
source: PAGOURO_BE/README.md (Status table: Our corpus 3,043 images); PAGOURO_PLAY/README.md (Pictures drawn by Pagouro BE)

title: Where the Posters Came From
text: The art model trained on posters from the Library of Congress, The Met Open Access and the Art Institute of Chicago. Every image has its own row in a public ledger.
source: PAGOURO_BE/README.md (What it is, said plainly: Our part is the corpus)

title: All Made Before 1929
text: Every poster Pagouro BE studied was made before 1929. Art that belongs to everyone, put to work teaching something new.

title: A Clean Starting Point
text: Pagouro BE is built on CommonCanvas, a base model trained only on Creative Commons photographs. It was chosen because its data has a license statement that holds up.

title: Yours to Keep
text: Pictures drawn by Pagouro BE are CC0. Print them, frame them, remix them. No permission needed; credit welcome.

title: No Watermark
text: Pagouro BE puts no watermark in its pictures. What it draws for you is yours.
source: PAGOURO_BE/README.md (Yours. Outputs are CC0. No watermark.)

title: Draws on Your Own Computer
text: Pagouro BE draws on an ordinary CPU, offline, from a USB stick. Nothing you type leaves the machine.

title: Patience Is Part of It
text: On an idle desktop, Pagouro BE paints a picture in about 95 seconds. On a small budget laptop, most of an hour. Either way, on your own machine.
source: PAGOURO_BE/README.md (Status: 95 s per picture on idle 16-core desktop; 52 min on Intel N100 laptop)

title: Under Ten Dollars
text: The fine-tune that taught Pagouro BE the poster style cost $7.72 of rented GPU time, read from the bill.
source: PAGOURO_BE/README.md (Status table: Training, $7.72 read from the bill)

title: Measured, Not Promised
text: Asked for a subject, Pagouro BE drew it in 34 of 40 pictures scored by a person. The test was written before training began.
source: PAGOURO_BE/docs/MODEL_CARD.md (The numbers on the box: subject drawn 34/40; gate committed before any training)

title: Honest About Its Flaws
text: Pagouro BE often adds lettering nobody asked for, and it can't be read. The box says so. A tool that names its flaws is one you can trust.
source: PAGOURO_BE/docs/MODEL_CARD.md (What it does badly; unasked lettering 136/160)

title: Not Retouched
text: The pictures in this game were not retouched or cropped by hand. What the model drew is what you're putting back together.
source: PAGOURO_BE/showcase/x180/README.md (Not retouched, not cropped, not filtered by hand); PAGOURO_PLAY/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (Assets: showcase pictures)

title: Signed and Timestamped
text: Pagouro BE 1.0 was signed, and its manifest timestamped in Bitcoin block 969239. Anyone can check that their copy is the real one.
source: PAGOURO_BE/README.md (Status: manifest signed, timestamped on Bitcoin block 969239)

title: Share-Alike Weights
text: The art model's weights are CC BY-SA 4.0: free to use, change and share, and what you build from them stays open too.

title: Six More Styles
text: Pagouro BE Styles adds six looks: Southwest rock art, ukiyo-e, Egyptian tomb painting, Greek vase painting, natural-history plates and Dutch painting.

title: Open Captions
text: Every training image in the Styles pack was described by an open-weights vision model, and each caption is labeled as such in its ledger.
source: PAGOURO_BE/docs/README_STYLES.md (Captions ... Qwen 3.6 27B, Apache 2.0, labelled in the ledgers)

title: Respect for the Sources
text: The rock-art style learned from photographs of ancestral sites in the American Southwest. The pack names its sources and claims nothing about the cultures' meanings.

title: It Learned the Scanner Too
text: Sometimes Pagouro BE paints a poster as if photographed in an archive, color strip and all. It learned from museum scans, and it learned the scanning.

title: If in Doubt, Out
text: Collections whose terms treat commercial and noncommercial use differently were left out of the art corpus. Only images free for everyone went in.
source: PAGOURO_BE/docs/CORPUS.md (What is not in it: Gallica left out; Our corpus: LoC no known restrictions, Met and AIC CC0)

title: Enlarged, Not Repainted
text: Pagouro BE paints at 512 pixels. These pictures were enlarged twice over by Real-ESRGAN, an openly licensed upscaler. Nothing was painted in by hand.
source: PAGOURO_BE/showcase/x180/README.md (Size: 2x Real-ESRGAN upscale, BSD-3 weights; not retouched)

title: Composed, Not Recorded
text: The piano you hear was composed by Pagouro Salon, a small model that writes music as notes. A free instrument plays them.

title: A Small Composer
text: The model that wrote this soundtrack has about 40 million parameters. It trained on one rented GPU in a session that cost about $3.80.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (round 1: model B ~40M params; pod about 2 h 24 min, about $3.80); runs/salon_r1/loop_v1/pagouro-salon-loop-v1.tracklist.json (model: round 1 model B)

title: Sixty-Two Minutes
text: The soundtrack is a 62-minute loop of 20 generated piano pieces, joined by short pauses so it repeats without a seam.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/runs/salon_r1/loop_v1/pagouro-salon-loop-v1.tracklist.json (minutes 62.1, pieces 20, gap 2.5 s); PAGOURO_SALON/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (Round 1c and the version 1 loop)

title: CC0 Music
text: Every note of this soundtrack is CC0. Put it in your own video, game or café. No permission needed.

title: The Piano Is Free Too
text: The piano sound is Upright Piano KW, a CC0 SoundFont from FreePats, played by FluidSynth, a free software synthesizer.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/runs/salon_r1/loop_v1/pagouro-salon-loop-v1.tracklist.json (soundfont Upright Piano KW (CC0, FreePats); renderer FluidSynth 2.6.1)

title: Learned From Public Scores
text: Pagouro Salon studied public-domain scores, including pieces typeset by volunteers at the Mutopia Project, each with its license recorded.

title: A Quarter Million Scores
text: Most of the pieces it learned from came from PDMX, a research dataset of more than 250,000 scores marked public domain, licensed CC BY 4.0.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md S-6; PAGOURO_SALON/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (751 PDMX + 230 Mutopia = 981 pieces)

title: A No Is a No
text: A fine digital edition of Joplin was turned down because its license forbade commercial use. Joplin's music is public domain and came in another way.

title: Notes, Not Old Records
text: Salon learned from scores, not old recordings, so it composes clean notes instead of imitating the hiss of a gramophone.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md S-1 (period recordings are acoustic 78s and would teach the model to sound like a gramophone)

title: Two Notes a Second
text: Puzzle music should move at about two notes a second, near the pace of Satie's first Gymnopédie. Busier pieces were slowed or left out.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md S-7; PAGOURO_SALON/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (Gymnopédie 1 at 2.0 notes/s; puzzle filter)

title: Tested by Ear
text: The first samples were judged too fast to puzzle to, so a rule was written: soft, slow, unhurried. The ear decided, and the numbers agreed.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md S-7; PAGOURO_SALON/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (Eric's listen, phrase-blocked samples)

title: No Endless Loops
text: Small music models tend to repeat themselves. Salon blocks exact repeats of any phrase about six notes long, which brought it closest to real Satie.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (Sampler sweep: block any repeated 24-token phrase, about six notes; closest to real Satie on both numbers)

title: Mistakes on the Record
text: One early Salon model learned to predict the wrong note entirely. The bug, the fix and the lesson are all written in the build log.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (Round 1a, a bug of mine, kept here)

title: The Salon Repertoire
text: Salon aims at the salon and café piano of about 1860 to 1920: Satie, Debussy, Fauré, Joplin and their neighbors.

title: Every Piece in the Ledger
text: No piece trained the composer until its source link, license, composer and date were written to the ledger first.

title: Same Seed, Same Song
text: Give Pagouro Salon the same seed and settings, and it composes the same piece again. Music you can reproduce exactly.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md S-1 (deterministic from a seed); PAGOURO_SALON/scripts/generate.py (docstring: Deterministic for a given seed)

title: Quietly Underneath
text: The soundtrack is evened out to a quiet level on purpose. It's there to keep you company, not to fill the room.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (loop evened to a quiet level); PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md S-7 (played softly)

title: Chopin and Other
text: The loop alternates pieces sampled under the model's Chopin and Other labels, the ones that won the listening test.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md S-7; PAGOURO_SALON/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (Round 1c: Chopin and Other labels first and alternating, as Eric preferred)

title: The Third Sibling
text: Pagouro Salon is the third member of the Pagouro family, after the text model and the poster model. Same rules: licensed, ledgered, measured.

title: Art Songs, Minus the Words
text: The next Salon round added the piano parts of 1,244 art songs from the CC0 OpenScore Lieder collection, vocal lines removed.

title: The Speed Dial
text: In round two, asking Salon for its slowest setting gave about 2.3 notes a second, the speed of the real Gymnopédies.
source: PAGOURO_SALON/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (Round 2b, B2L: the speed label steers)

title: The Hermit Crab
text: Pagouro comes from the Greek págouros, hermit crab: an animal that carries a home it did not build and can move out of.

title: The Ouroboros
text: The 'ouro' in Pagouro nods to the ouroboros, the loop that needs nothing from outside.

title: It Began With a Question
text: Could one person, with no GPU, build a language model from scratch and run it as a plain program? That question became Pagouro.

title: AI on a USB Stick
text: Pagouro is a one-billion-parameter language model that lives on a USB stick, runs offline, and needs nothing from outside.

title: Three Commitments
text: A named license for every training source. 'I don't know' instead of an invented answer, measured. And what you type stays on your machine.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/ORIGIN.md (three commitments); PAGOURO_BUILD/README.md (Licensed, source by source; post-publication note)

title: The Honest Numbers
text: On its frozen test, Pagouro invents an answer to 13% of unanswerable questions and answers 82% of real ones correctly. Both numbers, always together.

title: Run the Test Yourself
text: Pagouro's honesty test ships with it. Run it on Pagouro, then run it on the big models too.

title: Frozen Before It Existed
text: The test that measures Pagouro's honesty was written and frozen before the model existed, so it could not be bent to fit.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/WHY.md (Honest, measured); PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/facts.json (honesty.suite: frozen before the model existed)

title: A Thousandth the Size
text: Pagouro is roughly a thousandth the size of the models you already use. It knows less, and it's built to tell you when it doesn't know.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/WHY.md (The short answer); PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/DECISIONS.md D-50 (marketing language)

title: About 100 Billion Tokens
text: Pagouro read about 100 billion tokens of licensed, dated text: roughly a hundred for each of its 969 million parameters.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/facts.json (training.tokens 99,724,809,408; parameters 968,968,192); PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/WHY.md (a hundred tokens per parameter)

title: Before 2022
text: Everything Pagouro was pretrained on was written or collected before January 1, 2022, and every source row says how that date was established.

title: Sixty-One Hours
text: Pagouro's main training run took 61.6 hours on eight rented H100 GPUs, from September 22 to 24, 2026.

title: What It Cost
text: The training run cost $1,778.97, read from the account. About $1,900 of rented compute in all, by one person, and the result is free.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/README.md (Bill $1,778.97; built by one person, about $1,900 in rented compute); PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/facts.json (price_usd 0)

title: Finished on Purpose
text: Pagouro was released once, frozen, signed, and its hash anchored to Bitcoin. A finished thing can be checked by anyone, anywhere.

title: Your Words Are Yours
text: Pagouro puts no watermark in what it writes, and the project claims no rights in its outputs.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/WHY.md (your words are yours); PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/DECISIONS.md D-83

title: Private, Precisely
text: Your questions never leave this machine. This machine is still your responsibility.

title: No Account Needed
text: No account, no update check, no telemetry. Pagouro runs on the CPU of any 64-bit Windows, Linux or Mac computer.

title: Runs on a Budget Laptop
text: On a small Intel N100 laptop, Pagouro starts in about a minute and gives its first answer in 10 to 20 seconds.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/README.md (Running it: measured on an Intel N100 laptop)

title: Open Weights, Share-Alike
text: Pagouro's weights are CC BY-SA 4.0 and its code is Apache 2.0. Fork it, change it, share it.

title: The Full Recipe
text: Pagouro's full-precision checkpoints and its tokenizer are public on Hugging Face, so the next person can start where this one stopped.

title: The Book
text: Make Your Own AI tells the story of Pagouro, with the instructions in the same pages. The whole book is CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: Corrected in Public
text: When outside audits found claims stated too strongly, Pagouro said so in public. Nothing that shipped was altered; the record was corrected around it.

title: The Country That Isn't
text: Asked for the capital of Verdania, a country that doesn't exist, a small test model answered 'Verdania itself.' Catching that is what Pagouro's test is for.

title: Careful Mode
text: Type /careful and Pagouro asks itself each question five times. If the answers disagree, it calls the result a guess.

title: Text Only, and Says So
text: Pagouro reads and writes text only. The pictures in this game were drawn by its sibling, Pagouro BE.

title: A Person and an AI
text: Pagouro was made by Eric Wade with Claude, an AI assistant, and every decision along the way is written down with its date and reason.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/facts.json (made_by); PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md (preamble: every decision written down with the date)

title: A Copy That Stays
text: A permanent copy of Pagouro is stored on Arweave, and a mirror with every receipt lives on Quilibrium QStorage.

title: When Rights Were Unclear
text: When the rights to a source were unclear, the answer was no, and the ledger records what was removed and why.

title: A Working Minimum
text: Pagouro is free and fully open, a working minimum meant for someone with time, skills or money to make bigger.

title: Today's Puzzle
text: Everyone gets the same daily puzzle: 48 pieces, chosen from the date. It works offline; no server decides.

title: The Year in the Shuffle
text: The daily shuffle is seeded with the number 1888, the year Erik Satie wrote his Gymnopédies.

title: The Whimsical Cut
text: Pieces are cut fresh from a seed: round tabs, bulbous ones, mushroom caps and spiky arrowheads. Prefer tradition? Switch to Classic cut.

title: Every Edge Fits
text: The puzzle is cut as one shared lattice, so every edge belongs to two neighbors and they always fit exactly.

title: Change the Table
text: If the picture blends into the table, change it. All nine table colors come from the Belle Époque palette Pagouro uses everywhere.
source: PAGOURO_PLAY/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (Colors snapped to the locked house palette); PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/DECISIONS.md D-74

title: Free, Simply
text: Pagouro Jigsaw is free. No ads, no tracking, no account, no paid unlock. Just a quiet note that Pagouro made it.

title: Thirty Pictures
text: Thirty pictures come with the game, from lighthouses and steam trains to a black cat on a red cushion. Cut any of them into 12 to 150 pieces.

title: The Tray
text: Loose pieces wait in a two-row tray. Swipe sideways to browse, swipe a piece up to lift it onto the board.

title: Open Fonts
text: The lettering here is Cormorant Garamond and EB Garamond, both free under the SIL Open Font License.

title: Built in the Open
text: Pagouro Jigsaw is built with Godot, a free and open-source game engine. The game's own code is Apache 2.0.
source: PAGOURO_PLAY/README.md (Godot 4.7.2; Licenses: Code Apache 2.0); general (Godot is open source)

title: The Beautiful Era
text: Belle Époque, 'the beautiful era,' is the name later given to the years in France from the 1870s to the First World War.

title: A Name Given Looking Back
text: The Belle Époque ended in August 1914. People named it afterward, remembering a peace that had seemed permanent.

title: A Tower for a Fair
text: The Eiffel Tower was built as the entrance to the 1889 Exposition Universelle in Paris. Many artists of the day hated it at first.

title: The 1900 Exposition
text: The Paris Exposition of 1900 left the city the Grand Palais, the Petit Palais and the Pont Alexandre III.

title: The City of Light
text: Electric light spread through Paris in the Belle Époque, and the 1900 Exposition celebrated it with a Palace of Electricity.

title: The Métro Opens
text: Paris opened its first Métro line in 1900. Hector Guimard's entrances, all curling cast iron, still mark many stations.

title: Art Nouveau's Name
text: Art Nouveau took its name from a Paris shop: Siegfried Bing's Maison de l'Art Nouveau, opened in 1895.

title: The Whiplash Curve
text: Art Nouveau loved the whiplash curve: stems, hair and smoke that bend like a signature. The scrolls at this board's corners are a small nod to it.
source: general history; PAGOURO_PLAY/docs/BUILD_LOG.md (Art Nouveau scrolls at each corner)

title: Up in Montmartre
text: Montmartre, a hilltop village of windmills and cheap rents, became the heart of Paris night life and home to the artists who painted it.

title: The Moulin Rouge
text: The Moulin Rouge opened at the foot of Montmartre in 1889, a red windmill on its roof. Its posters became as famous as its dancers.

title: Le Chat Noir
text: Le Chat Noir, opened in 1881, was the Montmartre cabaret where poets, singers and painters met. Its black cat still prowls on posters today.

title: Satie at the Piano
text: Erik Satie played piano in Montmartre and wrote his Gymnopédies in 1888. Their unhurried pace set the tempo for this game's music.
source: general history; PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md S-7 (Gymnopédie 1 as the speed reference)

title: Ragtime Crosses the Sea
text: Scott Joplin published the Maple Leaf Rag in 1899. Ragtime soon charmed Paris; Debussy wrote a cakewalk of his own.

title: The First Picture Show
text: In December 1895 the Lumière brothers held the first paid public film screening, in a café in Paris.

title: The Bicycle Craze
text: In the 1890s the bicycle set Paris rolling. Women rode in bloomers, and bicycle makers covered the walls with posters.

title: Freedom to Post
text: France's press freedom law of 1881 opened the walls to the poster. Paris bloomed with color, except where 'Défense d'afficher' was painted.
source: general history (Law on the Freedom of the Press, 29 July 1881)

title: Poster Mania
text: Parisians caught affichomanie, poster mania. Some collectors peeled fresh posters off the walls before the paste was dry.

title: The Japanese Influence
text: Japanese woodblock prints poured into Paris in the late 1800s. Their flat color and bold outline shaped the posters of Toulouse-Lautrec, Bonnard and Mucha.

title: Drawing on Stone
text: Lithography, printing from a drawing on flat stone, was invented by Alois Senefelder in the 1790s. A century later it turned Paris into a gallery.

title: One Stone per Color
text: A color lithograph is printed one stone per color, each sheet passed through the press again and again, lined up exactly.

title: A Gallery in the Street
text: Before radio, the poster was the city's loudest voice. You didn't visit this art in a museum; you walked past it on the way to work.

title: Songs for a Drink
text: At a café-concert, anyone could hear a song for the price of a drink. Stars like Yvette Guilbert and Aristide Bruant became poster legends.

title: The Divine Sarah
text: Sarah Bernhardt was the most famous actress of her age, and she understood the power of a poster better than anyone.

title: The Salon
text: In a Belle Époque salon, music was played at home among friends. Pagouro Salon is named for the room this music was written for.
source: general history; PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md S-1 (Salon is the room the music was written for)

title: Selling the Journey
text: Railway companies sold the seaside and the Alps with posters. This game's trains, lighthouses and sailboats are in that tradition.

title: Crowds at the Fair
text: The 1900 Paris Exposition drew tens of millions of visitors, who came to see moving walkways, giant telescopes and the new century.

title: Jules Chéret
text: Jules Chéret is often called the father of the modern poster. His bright, dancing women filled the walls of Paris for decades.

title: Chéret's Yellow
text: The chrome yellow in this game's palette is named for Chéret's yellow, one of eight color ramps taken from the Paris poster.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md (palette table: chrome yellow, Chéret's yellow); PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/DECISIONS.md D-74

title: Mucha's Gismonda
text: Alphonse Mucha's Gismonda, for Sarah Bernhardt, went up on Paris walls at New Year 1895. Tall, gold and calm, it made him famous almost overnight.

title: Mucha's Colors
text: The sage green and dusty rose in this game are Mucha's colors, part of the Belle Époque palette Pagouro adopted for everything it makes.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md (sage: Mucha's green; dusty rose: Mucha's pink); PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/DECISIONS.md D-74

title: Toulouse-Lautrec's First
text: Toulouse-Lautrec's first poster, Moulin Rouge: La Goulue (1891), made a dance hall into an icon with flat color and black silhouettes.

title: The Most-Studied Artist
text: Toulouse-Lautrec is the artist with the most pictures in Pagouro BE's first training corpus: 365 of them.
source: PAGOURO_BE/docs/CORPUS.md (round 1: Top artists by image count, Toulouse-Lautrec 365)

title: Steinlen's Cats
text: Théophile-Alexandre Steinlen loved cats and drew them everywhere. His black cat for Le Chat Noir is one of the best-known posters ever made.

title: Eugène Grasset
text: Swiss-born Eugène Grasset brought medieval line and Art Nouveau ornament to posters, books, stained glass and even a typeface.

title: Bonnard's Champagne
text: Pierre Bonnard's first poster, France-Champagne (1891), so impressed Toulouse-Lautrec that he sought out its printer.

title: American Echoes
text: The poster craze crossed the Atlantic: Edward Penfield, Will Bradley and Louis Rhead made American posters in the 1890s. They taught Pagouro too.
source: general history; PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/DECISIONS.md D-74 (Penfield, Rhead, Bradley in the Met slice)

title: The Library of Congress
text: More than 1,500 of the art model's training posters come from the Library of Congress Artist Posters collection, marked 'no known restrictions.'
source: PAGOURO_BE/README.md (Our part: LoC Artist Posters, no known restrictions; Status table: LoC 1,515)

title: The Met's Gift
text: The Met shares its public-domain works as CC0 through Open Access. 533 of its prints and posters helped teach Pagouro BE.
source: PAGOURO_BE/README.md (The Met Open Access (CC0); Status table: Met 533)

title: The Art Institute of Chicago
text: 995 pictures from the Art Institute of Chicago's open-access collection, all CC0, went into the art model's training set.
source: PAGOURO_BE/README.md (Art Institute of Chicago CC0; Status table: AIC 995)

title: Flat Planes, Bold Lines
text: Pagouro's style brief is the Paris lithographic poster of 1890 to 1910: flat planes of color, a bold silhouette, hand-lettered titles.

title: Never Pure Black
text: In the Pagouro palette the outline is a warm black, never pure black, and the ground is poster cream, not white.

title: Thirty-Two Colors
text: Pagouro's look uses 32 colors in eight ramps: warm black and poster cream, chrome yellow and vermilion, Prussian blue, sage, dusty rose and gold.

title: Masters of the Poster
text: From 1895 to 1900, Les Maîtres de l'Affiche published small reprints of great posters every month, so anyone could own a collection.

title: Lettered by Hand
text: Belle Époque poster titles were drawn by hand, as part of the picture. Lettering is still the hardest thing for Pagouro BE to get right.
source: PAGOURO_BUILD/docs/DECISIONS.md D-74 (hand-lettered titles); PAGOURO_BE/docs/MODEL_CARD.md (asked-for words legible 0/6)

title: The Crab in the Medallion
text: Pagouro's mark is a hermit crab tucked into its shell, in a round medallion with Art Nouveau flourishes at the corners.

title: Toulouse-Lautrec and Bonnard
text: For Pagouro's first Belle Époque style model, the Met slice held 200 works by Toulouse-Lautrec and 125 by Bonnard.

title: Still Working
text: These posters once sold soap, champagne and cabaret tickets. More than a century later, in the public domain, they're teaching a new kind of artist.
source: general history; PAGOURO_BE/README.md (public-domain posters as training corpus)

title: Own Your AI
text: The best AI is one you can hold in your hand, run on your own machine and keep for as long as you like.

title: Open Weights
text: Open weights mean nobody can take the model back. Once it's on your stick, it's yours.

title: Everyone's Inheritance
text: The public domain belongs to everyone. Teaching new tools from it keeps it working for all of us.

title: Credit the Sources
text: Good AI names its sources. Every Pagouro model keeps a ledger of where its training came from.
source: none: opinion (first sentence); PAGOURO_BUILD/README.md, PAGOURO_BE/README.md, PAGOURO_SALON/docs/DECISIONS.md S-2 (ledgers)

title: Keep, Change, Share
text: A good license lets you keep it, change it and pass it on. Share-alike makes sure the next person can too.

title: Check, Don't Trust
text: Don't take an AI's promises on faith. Choose one whose claims you can check for yourself.

title: An Honest Answer
text: 'I don't know' is an answer. An honest small model can be worth more than a confident wrong one.

title: Small Is Beautiful
text: Not every AI needs a data center. Some of the most useful ones fit on a USB stick.

title: Finished Is a Feature
text: Software that never changes under you is a kind of freedom. A frozen release is a promise kept.

title: Fork It
text: If you'd build it differently, fork it. That's what open means.

title: A Tool Like Any Other
text: AI is a tool, like the litho stone and the printing press. The more hands it's in, the more art gets made.

title: Free as in Free
text: No ads, no tracking, no account. Some things can simply be free.
source: none: opinion; PAGOURO_PLAY/README.md (no ads, no tracking, no account)

title: Nothing Sent, Nothing Logged
text: When your questions never leave your computer, there's nothing for a provider to log.

title: Made With AI, Proudly
